what: full-table completion: the five remaining compared-table columns (RefCOCO testA/testB, RefCOCO+ testA/testB, RefCOCOg test(u)) evaluated with the same frozen components and the aligned protocol
protocol: mIoU = mean per-expression IoU; oIoU = pooled intersection/union, both from the per-expression records under the aligned protocol of protocol_audit.json; sentence-prompt box prior (the shipped rule)
published_source: GLOD-RIS Table I, test columns (same source as the audited val columns in protocol_audit.json)
pareto_ledger: Scoped precisely: the shipped method strictly exceeds the published GLOD-RIS row on 5/5 test-column mIoU values and 5/5 test-column oIoU values (both transcribed from GLOD-RIS Table I test columns, the oIoU blocks verified against the known val oIoU before transcription), plus the three val mIoU and three val oIoU values (aligned re-evaluations, protocol_audit.json). GLOD-RIS does not report gRefCOCO, so our gRefCOCO results are compared there against the same-class floors (PSALM ECCV 2024 Table 12: 42.0 cIoU / 43.3 gIoU; SELF1E-8B CVPR 2026 arXiv:2603.19026: 44.4 cIoU, the higher cIoU floor per the 2026-10-08 escalation rule) and the run's own prior record, per the 2026-10-08 operator standard -- not against GLOD-RIS. Beyond the mIoU/oIoU table, the ledger carries: reproducibility (their published numbers do not reproduce on our independent implementation: -25.7/-23.1/-20.6 mIoU vs the val columns, glodris_repro.json, ruled also causally by the same-pool rule swap) and API-independence (our path is fully local; GLOD-RIS's inference depends on a network MLLM API). N_acc/T_acc for the shipped gRefCOCO row live in main_grefcoco.json (86.14/87.85). One axis is not dominated and stays declared: the gRefCOCO path adds a second frozen detector next to the VLM prior.
